title: Up
label: Needwant
yt_title: Mario Basanov - Up (Original Mix) - Needwant Records
why: Same remixer as the Stand Still remix: Mario Basanov's own Needwant single (Up EP, 2010) — the same warm, rubbery Lithuanian deep-house bounce and sunny, slightly off-kilter chords that make his Flight Facilities rework so strange and lovely.

title: We Are Child Of Love
label: Needwant
yt_title: Mario Basanov - We Are Child Of Love (The Mekanism Remix)
why: Mario Basanov vocal tune on Needwant, the label that broke him; the Mekanism remix keeps the dreamy, wide-eyed vocal and adds a disco-house groove — same feel-good melancholy as the Stand Still remix.

title: Damn Girl
label: Needwant
why: Basanov in playful mode on Needwant: a cheeky, chopped vocal hook over a jazzy deep-house swing — the quirky, characterful side of the man behind the Stand Still remix.

title: Slip Away
why: Mario Basanov with a soulful, floating Rahjwanti vocal — the same blend of warmth and wistful vocal melody he gave Micky Green on Stand Still.
notes: Official extended version (8:01) uploaded by Mood Music: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h5V4OWi-R7g

title: Under Your Feet
label: Needwant
yt_title: Mario Basanov ft. Jazzu - Under Your Feet
why: Basanov with Lithuania's Jazzu on Needwant — her smoky, slightly odd phrasing over his bouncy, organ-flecked deep house is the closest cousin to Micky Green's dreamy vocal on the Stand Still remix.
notes: Needwant's own upload is only a 2:00 preview (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sQ_QTHxOIg4); unofficial full-length upload used.

title: I'll Be Gone
label: Silence Music
yt_title: I'll Be Gone feat. Jazzu (Extended Original)
why: The Lithuanian deep-house anthem: Mario Basanov & Vidis with Jazzu on Silence Music (SILENCE005, 2009). Hazy, lovelorn vocal and soft chords — the blueprint for the bittersweet Basanov sound on Stand Still.
notes: Longer Mario Basanov & Vidis Redo (8:14) exists on the same EP.

title: Changed
why: Mario & Vidis again, this time with Ernesto's yearning, slightly strange male vocal — melodic Baltic deep house with the same emotional pull as the Stand Still remix.

title: Who's Shot The Silence?!
label: Silence Music
yt_title: Who's Shot The Silence?! feat. Jazzu (Album Redo)
why: The title alone is quirky: Mario Basanov, Vidis and Jazzu on their own Silence Music label — jazzy, offbeat vocal deep house straight from the Vilnius scene that produced the Stand Still remix.
notes: Short-ish (4:34); 8:10 fan upload of the redo: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g364gd8ifGE

title: Corinne
label: Because Music
why: Basanov does exactly what he did to Flight Facilities: takes a quirky indie-pop song (Metronomy, The English Riviera era, Because Music 2011) and turns it into a warm, groovy deep-house cut with the odd vocal left intact. Perfect partner track.

title: Changes
label: Om Records
why: Another Mario Basanov remix of a vocal band (Crazy P on Om Records): Danielle Moore's soulful vocal over his trademark sunny, rolling disco-house — same remix formula as Stand Still.

title: Space Me Out
label: Silence Music
yt_title: Space Me Out feat. Egle Sirvydyte (Mario Basanov Remix)
why: Lithuanian connection: Mario Basanov remixing Vilnius band Downtown Party Network on Silence Music, with Eglė Sirvydytė's spacey, dreamy female vocal — the most direct sibling of the Stand Still remix.

title: Can't Believe
label: Needwant
yt_title: Needw020 - The Mekanism - Can't Believe (Mario Basanov Remix)
why: Early Mario Basanov remix on Needwant (NEEDW020): pitched, soulful vocal snippets over jazzy deep-house keys — the warm Needwant sound that leads straight to Stand Still.
notes: Mario Basanov Dub (8:03) also on Needwant: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VqyAXTdvwlQ

title: Walking With Elephants
yt_title: Ten Walls - Walking with Elephants (Original Mix)
why: Lithuanian like Mario Basanov: Ten Walls' 2014 crossover with that strange, fanfare-like brass riff — quirky, melodic and huge, the eccentric streak Robin hears in the Stand Still remix.
notes: Official Ten Walls upload is a short video edit (3:02): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tuMgJrFoAFY; unofficial full-length used.

title: Clair De Lune
label: Future Classic
yt_title: Flight Facilities - Clair De Lune feat. Christine Hoberg
why: The Flight Facilities single right before Stand Still (Future Classic, 2012): seven-plus minutes of slow-motion, starry nu-disco with a dreamy female vocal — same artists, same label, same wistful glow.

title: Pizza Guy
label: Future Classic
why: Future Classic labelmate of Flight Facilities; slap-bass, goofy title and a sunny, cheeky groove — the label's quirky, characterful side, just like the Stand Still remix.

title: I'll Get You
chart_source: Curated: Flight Facilities fans also like
why: LA duo Classixx with a lovelorn, slightly naive vocal over glossy nu-disco — the same sweet pop-meets-dancefloor feel as Micky Green on Stand Still.
notes: Short (4:06); no official extended upload found.

title: In The End (I Want You To Cry)
label: Running Back
yt_title: In the End (I Want You to Cry)
why: Tensnake's 2009 Running Back breakthrough (RB015): a heartbreak vocal loop and filtered disco chords that are joyous and sad at once — the bittersweet mood of the Stand Still remix.
release: In The End (I Want You To Cry)

title: Blind
label: DFA
why: Antony Hegarty's eerie, trembling vocal is as strange and special as it gets; Frankie Knuckles' remix (DFA, 2008) makes it a warm, swinging house classic — quirky vocal + deep groove, the Stand Still formula.

title: Flutes
label: Domino
why: Hot Chip (Domino, 2012) are kings of the oddball vocal; Sasha stretches Flutes into a hypnotic, melodic house journey — weird, warm and danceable, like Basanov's take on Stand Still.

title: In The Morning
label: Domino
why: Jeremy Greenspan's fragile falsetto, remixed by Hot Chip into a long, bubbling dancefloor cut (Domino) — indie vocal turned deep and groovy, exactly what Basanov did with Micky Green.

title: Beautiful Life
label: Kompakt
why: Kompakt pop at its finest: Gui Boratto's 2007 Chromophobia anthem, with his wife Luciana Villanova's whispered, almost naive vocal floating over shimmering melody — beautiful-strange like Stand Still.

title: Minimal
label: Kompakt
yt_title: Matias Aguayo - Minimal (DJ Koze Mix) - 20 Jahre Kompakt Kollektion 1 CD1
why: Kompakt oddity: Matias Aguayo's mumbled, playful vocal reworked by DJ Koze into a bouncy, melodic groover — the kind of characterful vocal twist Robin loves in the Stand Still remix.

title: Loreley
label: Kompakt
why: Kölsch's 1977 album (Kompakt, 2013): a naive, music-box-like melody that is equal parts joyful and melancholic — the same emotional, slightly whimsical feel as the Stand Still remix.

title: Goldfisch
label: Kompakt
why: Also from Kölsch's 1977 (Kompakt, 2013): a cheeky, catchy melodic hook and warm bassline — quirky melodic house with a smile, sitting nicely next to Basanov's Stand Still remix.

title: Happiness
label: Kompakt
why: Kompakt's dreamy pop-house: Superpitcher's hazy, half-sung vocal over a soft, swaying groove — strange and tender, the same mood as Micky Green over Basanov's chords.
notes: Michael Mayer Mix (8:26) also on Topic: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r815crvfTp8

title: Without You
label: Crosstown Rebels
why: Crosstown Rebels' deeper side (CRM064, 2010): Kenny Glasgow's crooned, haunted vocal over a slinky deep-house groove — moody, soulful and offbeat like the Stand Still remix.
notes: Topic upload may be an edit (5:16); full-length (8:39) fan upload of the Crosstown release: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yy1iGRxDlHk

title: Summertime
label: Crosstown Rebels
why: Jamie Jones on Crosstown Rebels with Norwegian duo Ost & Kjex's playful, slightly odd vocal — sunny, melodic and a bit odd, very much the Stand Still vibe.

title: Vibe Your Love
label: Crosstown Rebels
why: Early Maceo Plex on Crosstown Rebels: a pitched, sensual vocal and lush deep-house melody — warm and a little uncanny, like the Basanov remix of Stand Still.

title: Can't Leave You
label: Crosstown Rebels
why: From Maceo Plex's Sweating Tears EP (Crosstown Rebels CRM082): a plaintive, looped love-sick vocal and rolling bass — emotional deep house with a characterful twist.

title: Forward Motion
label: Hot Creations
chart_source: Curated: Hot Creations early deep vocal
why: Early Hot Creations (HOTC008, 2011): Jamie Jones & Lee Foss with Ali Love's dreamy, slightly detached vocal over a warm deep groove — vocal deep house with character, like Stand Still.

title: Reverse Skydiving
label: Hot Creations
chart_source: Curated: Hot Creations early deep vocal
why: Hot Natured on Hot Creations (2013) with Anabel Englund's breathy, dreamy vocal and a quirky title — the sweet pop-vocal-meets-deep-house balance of the Stand Still remix.

title: Destiny
label: Permanent Vacation
why: From John Talabot's fIN (Permanent Vacation, 2012): Pional's soft, melancholic vocal over tropical, Balearic house — dreamy, unusual and danceable, a perfect fit next to Stand Still.

title: It's All Over
label: Hivern Discs
why: Pional on Talabot's Hivern Discs: a fragile, sad vocal over warm, glowing deep house — the same bittersweet vocal-led feel as Micky Green on the Basanov remix.

title: Primative People
label: Permanent Vacation
chart_source: Curated: Mano Le Tough / Tale Of Us early
yt_title: Mano Le Tough - Primative People (Tale Of Us Remix)
why: Permanent Vacation release: Mano Le Tough's soft, folky vocal remixed by early Tale Of Us into a melancholic, melodic deep cut — the dreamy, emotional side of Stand Still.

title: Snooze 4 Love
label: Running Back
yt_title: Todd Terje - Snooze 4 Love - Running Back RBCR-78
why: Todd Terje on Running Back: a woozy, sleepy synth melody and lazy disco groove — whimsical, warm and strange in the best way, sharing Stand Still's quirky charm.
notes: Dixon Remix (7:29) on Todd Terje's channel: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kp15oENs7lQ

title: Trainmann
label: Running Back
why: Running Back again: Tensnake turns Lauer's Trainmann into a filtered, French-touch disco cruiser — euphoric and a bit goofy, matching the Stand Still remix's playful warmth.

title: Brian Le Bon
label: Live At Robert Johnson
why: Roman Flügel on Live At Robert Johnson (PLAYRJC006): a strange, playful melody and gently swinging groove — eccentric, warm deep house in the Stand Still spirit.

title: Rej
label: Innervisions
why: Innervisions IV02 (2005): Âme's hypnotic, melodic deep-house classic — patient, warm and quietly strange, the deeper backbone behind remixes like Basanov's Stand Still.

artist: Henrik Schwarz, Âme, Dixon, Derrick L. Carter
title: Where We At
label: Innervisions
yt_title: IV05 Henrik Schwarz / Âme / Dixon feat. Derrick L. Carter - Where We At Version 1 - Where We At EP
why: Innervisions IV05: Henrik Schwarz, Âme and Dixon with Derrick Carter's odd, conversational vocal — jazzy, quirky deep house with a human twist, close kin to the Stand Still remix.

title: Body Language
label: Get Physical
yt_title: M.A.N.D.Y. vs Booka Shade - Body Language
why: Get Physical 2005 classic: that springy, cartoonish melody and whispered vocal — quirky, melodic and timeless, the Get Physical side of the Stand Still mood.

title: Hausch
why: Andhim's 'super house' (on Get Physical's channel): a cheeky, bouncy and melodic groove — playful and characterful like the Basanov remix.

title: Every Minute Alone
label: Life and Death
yt_title: WhoMadeWho - Every Minute Alone (Tale Of Us Remix)
why: Danish band WhoMadeWho's wistful vocal turned into slow-burning melodic house by early Tale Of Us on Life and Death — an indie vocal reworked for the floor, just like Stand Still.

title: Dark Song
why: Early Tale Of Us: a mournful, dreamy mood over a slow, melodic deep groove — the darker, more emotional mirror of the Stand Still remix's wistfulness.

title: I Can't Kick This Feeling When It Hits
label: KDJ
yt_title: I Can't Kick This Feeling When It Hits
why: Moodymann on his KDJ label: a looped, soulful sample and dusty, warm Detroit groove — soulful, odd and deeply human, the raw ancestor of Basanov's warm vocal house.

title: Insides
label: Ghostly International
why: Fort Romeau on Ghostly International (2015): woozy, dreamlike textures and lush synths over a deep groove — dreamy and unusual like Stand Still.

title: Mango
label: BPitch Control
why: Sascha Funke on BPitch Control: a twinkling, melancholy melody (later famous via Berlin Calling) over a minimal-deep groove — sweet, strange and danceable.

title: Magical Boy
label: Pampa
why: From DJ Koze's Amygdala (Pampa, 2013): Matthew Dear's deep, strange baritone over Koze's warm, wonky house — about as 'great, special and strange' as house music gets.

title: Purple Drank
label: Pampa
why: Axel Boman on DJ Koze's Pampa (PAMPA004): a woozy, syrupy-slow feel and loose, jazzy groove — quirky, characterful deep house in the spirit of the Stand Still remix.

title: Little People (Black City)
label: Ghostly International
why: Matthew Dear's Black City (Ghostly International, 2010): a nine-minute, oddly sensual vocal groove — strange and seductive, with the same indie-vocal-meets-deep-house DNA as Stand Still.

title: Final Credits
why: Midland's emotional house anthem: a soaring, nostalgic vocal and warm chords — big-hearted and bittersweet, the same feeling Robin gets from the Basanov remix.
